title: Primary CNS lymphoma
subtitle: A curable brain tumour if you get a clean diagnosis — no steroids before biopsy, a high-dose methotrexate backbone, and thiotepa-based transplant consolidation for the fit. The recurring trade-off is cure versus neurotoxicity
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin — primary CNS and HIV-associated lymphoma · NCCN · IPCG · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: What it is
items: DLBCL confined to brain, leptomeninges, spinal cord or eyes, no systemic disease. Almost all are non-GCB / ABC-type, with MYD88 L265P and CD79B mutations — the reason BTK inhibitors and lenalidomide work
WHO-HAEM5 groups it as primary large B-cell lymphoma of immune-privileged sites (with vitreoretinal and testicular); ICC keeps primary DLBCL of the CNS
Median age late 60s. Immunodeficiency (HIV, transplant) → EBV-driven disease, often multifocal and ring-enhancing
Classic MRI: homogeneously enhancing periventricular / deep lesion, restricted diffusion. Presents with focal deficits, personality change, raised ICP

blocks.heading: Diagnosis
items: AVOID CORTICOSTEROIDS BEFORE BIOPSY unless herniation is imminent — steroids lyse lymphoma cells and the lesion can vanish (“ghost tumor”), leaving a non-diagnostic biopsy. If already given and biopsy is negative, stop them and re-image
Stereotactic needle biopsy is the procedure — resection adds nothing and is not the goal
Tissue substitutes if biopsy is unsafe: CSF cytology + flow cytometry (and MYD88 L265P) or vitrectomy for vitreous involvement

blocks.heading: Staging — IPCG extent-of-disease workup
rows: MRI with gadolinium (+ spine MRI if symptoms or CSF+)
Slit-lamp + dilated fundus exam by ophthalmology — vitreoretinal disease changes local therapy and follow-up
LP if safe (no mass effect): cytology, flow, protein (protein feeds the IELSG score)
PET/CT (or CT C/A/P) · testicular exam ± ultrasound in men · marrow biopsy selectively
HIV, HBV/HCV, LDH, creatinine clearance (MTX eligibility), albumin, and look for effusions/ascites

boxes: avoid WBRT — neurotoxicity worst in elderly
ASCT if chemosensitive and not done · WBRT

blocks.heading: Prognostic scores
rows: 1 point each: age >60 · ECOG >1 · LDH ↑ · CSF protein ↑ · deep brain (periventricular, basal ganglia, brainstem, cerebellum). 2-yr OS 0–1: 80% · 2–3: 48% · 4–5: 15%
Class 1 age <50 · class 2 ≥50 + KPS ≥70 · class 3 ≥50 + KPS <70 — survival falls stepwise; needs only age and KPS

blocks.heading: Consolidation — the transplant vs radiation question
rows: WBRT vs thiotepa-ASCT after the induction randomization: 2-yr PFS 80% vs 69%, P=0.17 — equivalent disease control, but cognitive decline after WBRT
Age ≤60, randomized phase 2: 2-yr PFS 63% WBRT vs 87% ASCT; cognition impaired after WBRT, preserved after ASCT; toxic deaths 1 vs 5
MT-R-A then thiotepa/BCNU-ASCT vs EA: 2-yr PFS 73% vs 51% (P=0.02), but 28% of the EA arm progressed/died in induction; landmark from consolidation 86% vs 71%, NS
Phase 3, n=229, MATRix ×4 then ASCT vs R-DeVIC: 3-yr PFS 78% vs 51%, HR 0.43; OS HR 0.46 (5-yr 84% vs 63%). Fatal events 5 vs 2 — settles ASCT as the standard for fit patients
blocks.footnote: WBRT remains effective but the late leukoencephalopathy, ataxia and dementia make it the last choice for anyone likely to be cured — if used after CR, reduced-dose 23.4 Gy (R-MPV protocol).

blocks.heading: Elderly and unfit — what is known
rows: ≥60 yr, randomized phase 2 (non-comparative): MPV-A vs MTX-temozolomide — 1-yr PFS 36% in both; median OS 31 vs 14 mo; no late neurotoxicity without WBRT
≥65 yr, R-MP(L) + procarbazine maintenance: CR 36%, 2-yr PFS 37%, OS 47%
539 patients ≥60: combination HD-MTX beat MTX ± R (3-yr PFS 55% with MT-R vs 30%); maintenance 3-yr PFS 65% vs 45% — retrospective

blocks.heading: Relapsed / refractory agents
rows: iLOC phase 2 (n=52): response 52% ITT (CR 19%) at 2 mo, median PFS 4.8 mo; reaches CSF. Invasive aspergillosis reported (1 fatal). MSKCC phase 1: 10/13 responded. Off-label in the US
PROSPECT phase 2 (n=48): ORR 67%, CR 44%, median PFS 6.0 mo (ASCO 2025 abstract). Approved in Japan; US NDA under accelerated review, PDUFA 18 Dec 2026 — would be the first US-approved BTKi for PCNSL
REVRI phase 2 (n=50): ORR 36% at end of induction, median PFS 7.8 mo. Lenalidomide maintenance after salvage prolonged response (UCSF, Blood Adv 2018)
Reasonable if the prior response lasted >12 months
blocks.footnote: R/R responses are frequent but short — consolidate a second remission (ASCT if not yet done, or maintenance) wherever possible.

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — regimen dosing, high-dose methotrexate administration, supportive care, and the trials

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing (mg/m² unless stated)
rows: Rituximab 375 d−5 and d0 · MTX 3500 d1 (over 3–4 h) · cytarabine 2000 q12h ×4 d2–3 · thiotepa 30 d4 — q21d ×4, G-CSF. Age 18–70

Rituximab 500 d1 · MTX 3500 + vincristine 1.4 (handbook cap 2.8 mg) d2 · procarbazine 100 PO d1–7 odd cycles (low-tyramine diet) — q14d ×5; PR → 7 cycles. CR → WBRT 23.4 Gy, then cytarabine 3000 d1–2 ×2
MTX 8000 over 4 h d1 q14d ×8 · rituximab 375 ×6 doses · temozolomide 150 PO d7–11 every other cycle. Then EA: etoposide 40 mg/kg CIV over 96 h + cytarabine 2000 q12h ×8 d1–4
MTX 3500–8000 over 4 h q14d + rituximab 375 — elderly / frail backbone
Thiotepa-based conditioning: carmustine + thiotepa (IELSG32/43, Alliance 51101) or thiotepa + busulfan + cyclophosphamide (PRECIS, MSKCC)
Lenalidomide 15 mg daily (handbook) · procarbazine 100 mg/day ×5 d q4wk (PRIMAIN) · temozolomide 150 d1–5 q28d (Reni)
Rituximab 375 + temozolomide (handbook) · temozolomide alone 150 d1–5 q28d · WBRT
blocks.footnote: MT-R and EA dosing per CALGB 50202 (handbook lists EA etoposide as 10 mg/kg/day CIV d1–4, i.e. the same 40 mg/kg total). Prednisolone 1% eye drops with every HD-cytarabine.

blocks.heading: Supportive care
items: After the biopsy, dexamethasone freely for edema, then taper; PJP prophylaxis on prolonged steroids (atovaquone around MTX)
Antiseizure drugs only if seizures — no prophylaxis; prefer non-enzyme-inducing agents
VTE is common in PCNSL; weigh anticoagulation against the post-biopsy bleeding window
Neurocognitive baseline and follow-up; MRI q3 mo ×2 yr, then less often (late relapses happen)

blocks.heading: High-dose methotrexate — administration
rows: CrCl ≥50 mL/min for full dose (50% if 10–50; omit <10). No third-space fluid — drain or avoid with pleural effusion, ascites, edema (MTX sequesters and leaks back, prolonging exposure)
PPIs · TMP-SMX · NSAIDs / salicylates · penicillins · probenecid (and levetiracetam has case reports) — hold PJP TMP-SMX until the level clears

Half-normal saline + 100 mEq NaHCO₃/L at 500 mL/h ×2 h, then 125 mL/h. Do not start until urine pH ≥7 and UOP >100 mL/h; keep pH ≥7 until level <0.05–0.1 µM (MTX precipitates in acid urine). Rescue: NaHCO₃ bolus or acetazolamide
PCNSL protocols start 24 h after MTX start (25 mg IV q6h, or 100 mg/m² after 8 g/m² MT-R) — vs 36 h after the 24-h Burkitt infusion. Continue until MTX <0.05 µM

Daily from 24 h, with Cr and UOP. Escalate leucovorin (100 mg/m² q6h) for a Cr rise >50% or levels above the protocol curve — handbook thresholds (24-h infusion): >20 µM at 24 h, >1 at 48 h, >0.1 at 72 h; 4-h PCNSL infusions run on their own nomogram
50 U/kg IV once for level >1 µM with delayed clearance from renal failure. No leucovorin within 2 h either side; immunoassay unreliable for 48 h (DAMPA cross-reacts) — use chromatographic assay
AKI · transaminitis (common, transient) · mucositis · myelosuppression · acute / subacute encephalopathy (stroke-like; consider aminophylline, dextromethorphan)

blocks.heading: Special situations
items: HIV-associated PCNSL is EBV-driven and arises with advanced immunosuppression. Differential is toxoplasmosis — toxo serology, CSF EBV PCR, and biopsy if lesions fail to shrink on empiric anti-toxoplasma therapy. Treat with ART + HD-MTX-based therapy with curative intent (handbook: continue or start ART during chemotherapy)

Vitreoretinal involvement: systemic HD-MTX reaches the eye inconsistently — add intravitreal MTX or rituximab, or ocular RT if it persists (handbook: orbital RT or ophthalmology referral for intra-ocular therapy)
Response (IPCG): CR requires no enhancing disease, off steroids ≥2 weeks, a normal eye exam and negative CSF cytology — steroid-driven shrinkage is not a response

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: MTX ± HD-cytarabine: CR 46% vs 18% — established the doublet
+ rituximab + thiotepa: CR 49% vs 23%; 7-yr OS 56% vs 21%; 6% toxic deaths. Randomized phase 2
MT-R → EA, no WBRT, single arm: CR 66%, 2-yr PFS 57%
ASCT vs R-DeVIC after MATRix: 3-yr PFS 78% vs 51%; OS HR 0.46. Phase 3
ASCT ≥ WBRT or EA for disease control; WBRT costs cognition
Ibrutinib, R2 and tirabrutinib in R/R disease

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: Steroids before biopsy are the #1 avoidable diagnostic failure
Urine alkalinization is mandatory for HD-MTX (the opposite of TLS, where it is harmful)
Intrathecal chemotherapy is generally omitted when systemic MTX ≥3 g/m² is given — no benefit shown in retrospective series (R-MPV adds Ommaya MTX only for positive CSF)
Testicular exam in every man — testicular DLBCL can seed the CNS and changes the diagnosis
Rituximab is contested: it raised CR in IELSG32, but HOVON 105/ALLG NHL 24 (phase 3, n=199) found no EFS benefit (1-yr EFS 52% vs 49%, HR 1.00) — it stays in most regimens anyway
